messages:
nina: Heads up — ran a 8k RPS smoke today and saw a regressed p99 on the host path (~2x vs baseline). Attaching quick flame. :confused:
sam: any change in batcher or kernel selector lately?
leo: we rolled in the small-session bias last Thursday (batch_hint=min(32, tokens)) — could nudge kernel to scalar for more requests.
nina: pprof top samples (percent):
```
 31.0%  host_proxy::flush_small_writes
 16.5%  grpc::internal::stream_flush
 13.7%  tokenizer::tokenize_bytes
 10.2%  kvcache::lookup_miss_work
  7.1%  socket::writev_overhead
```
priya: flush_small_writes that dominant indicates we are doing many syscalls; maybe gateway flush_every=1ms?
dan: gateway was on low-latency mode for the experiment (flush_interval=1). Also saw more tiny HTTP/1.1 requests in traces.
leo: small sessions + aggressive gateway flusher -> lots of tiny frames. writev coalescing can't keep up. Kernel selector flip to scalar adds CPU per-token.
sam: can we reproduce locally with workload generator? Matrix: flush_interval={1,5,20}ms, batch_hint={32,64,auto}, kvcache_grouping={off,on}.
perf-bot: perf-run #175461 kicked off: matrix params above. Artifacts will land in ~30m.
priya: mitigation idea: host-proxy coalescer: buffer up to 6ms or 16KB before forwarding; also make kernel selector consult expected_batch_size hint to avoid scalar fallback for expected joins.
dan: try coalescer=6ms + kernel_expectation_override=vector for seq_len<40 on canary.
leo: also enable kvcache session-grouping so prefixes from same session are colocated and avoid key fragmentation.
nina: pushed coalescer=6ms + ksel_override for canary; running 8k RPS job now. Capture pprof + kvcache_metrics + kernel_decision_trace.
perf-bot: canary perf-run #175461 finished: artifacts -> https://ci.internal/perf/175461/artifacts
leo: quick summary from artifacts: tail latency reduced ~30%, writev_overhead samples dropped ~4x, kvcache hitrate recovered from 70% -> 90% under load. Kernel decision trace shows vector kernels chosen ~82% of requests vs 44% baseline.
priya: any downside? higher p95 CPU? memory?
dan: no memory change. CPU tail improved because vector kernels amortize overhead; slight increase in single-core burstiness but within headroom.
sam: good. Next steps: prod canary rollout of coalescer and ksel tweak, and follow-up RFC: make kernel selector batch-aware and add adaptive kvcache grouping. Also add alert rule on host_proxy::flush_small_writes p50/p95 ratio.
nina: I'm creating the RFC + will add links to perf artifacts. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
